Verdict

Reviewed 28 Oct 2026 · next 26 Jan 2027

WebGL renderer for large graphs, with the graphology ecosystem. MIT, active, 110 KB gzip, 6.9 MB and 10 packages. No provenance, and it needs WebGL2 and browser globals at import, so use it only in client components.

Current Reviewed version 4.0.4 Requirement: Graph visualization in a React application

Reasoning

  1. MIT and a public repository; 4.0.4 published 2026-10-27 with 14 releases in 90 days.
  2. WebGL rendering handles graphs far larger than a canvas renderer.
  3. 110 KB gzip with graphology; 6.9 MB install and 10 packages.
  4. No OSV advisories for 4.0.4 or graphology 0.26.0.
  5. React integration is available via @react-sigma/core 6.0.0 (MIT, active, peers sigma ^4 and graphology ^0.26).

Caveats

  • No npm provenance and no publish workflow; releases are manual.
  • Importing sigma in Node fails with 'WebGL2RenderingContext is not defined'. It must be dynamically imported or used in a client component.
  • No built-in layouts: pair it with graphology-layout-forceatlas2 or another layout package.
  • The React wrapper is a separate package with its own release cadence.

Decision context

Approved

cytoscape is the primary choice for Graph visualization in a React application. This package is classified as Adopted.

The NVL suite is denied: its LICENSE.txt limits use to Neo4j Aura or commercial Neo4j, it publishes no repository, carries no provenance and cannot be loaded by Node in either module system. 1.2.2 was checked separately: same licence and packaging, different layout stack, so the denial applies to both. Adopt Cytoscape.js as the primary renderer: MIT, zero dependencies, SLSA provenance, active, 138 KB gzip, and layouts via extensions. Use the core API with a ref or a thin internal wrapper because react-cytoscapejs is stale. Adopt Sigma.js as the fallback for large graphs: MIT, WebGL, 110 KB gzip and active, but client-only (WebGL2) and without provenance; pair it with graphology and @react-sigma/core. Hold @antv/g6 (88 MB, 104 packages, 413 KB gzip, 333 open issues, no release in 90 days) and @xyflow/react (excellent node editor, but not an exploration or layout engine).
